I am a licensed Loan Officer and recently ran into an audit finding with UWM on a previous client. This part is information prior to my loan which I believe can be beneficial to the entire complaint. The audit team asked for documents and proof of the properties being rented to offset his XXXX so the outcome of his approval wouldn't change. About a week later they notified us that he has been black listed for undisclosed properties after the property had been sold and the loan paid in full. I relayed the information to him with their decision. It turns out that the other properties were with UWM as well through a different Loan officer in another state. UWM ( United Wholesale Mortgage ) systems for checks and balances should have triggered or caught this in my opinion. If all of his info is on each property how did UWM not catch thi s prior to them closing back to back? This shows severe issues in the UWM system process which puts the consumer at risk. Not to mention it puts UWM at risk as well. This is when things really started showing up at my door step. A few months later I needed to refinance my own property. I started to notice or feel that I was being targeted and wondered if I myself had been flagged due to the previous incident. In a nutshell I was pushed over to having a higher rate and payment do to negligence of the UWM team. We clearly know this is illegal and is a ploy for UWM to make more money with me being at a higher rate. At closing I signed the anti steering document as there was no steering by XXXX Mortgage, I feel confident that there was steering by the underwriters to push me into products that would have been more beneficial for the company. I will explain this further below as I explain the series of events. On another occasion the underwriter requested a CPA letter. I gladly reached out and copied the exact request from underwriting that I received from the processor and sent it over to my CPA. United Wholesale Mortgage is currently processing a loan application for a mutual client and we were provided a CPA explanation letter on your letterhead and bearing your signature. Your assistance is appreciated. Please feel free to reach out directly with any questions or concerns. It appears this was perfectly set up to try and entrap me and again to deny the loan. The font in the letter is slightly different. However, there is a repeated trend in how my account is being handled by UWM. This appears to be Overt Evidence and a violation of fair lending. Let 's move on to credit accounts with installments less than 10 months. UWM refused to make changes though statements proved that there were less than 10 months. As defined under Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ( RESPA ) Fair Debt Collection Practices Act as well as the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), it is required that all accounting be applied based on actual amounts that are due. I have been paying an extra {$600.00} to {$700.00} per month towards negative escrow, which has not been applied accordingly. The monthly statements issued by SLS show that the minimum monthly payments due are {$1600.00}. The principal payment is {$200.00}, with interest being {$360.00} per month, which leaves the balance {$1000.00} to be applied to escrow ( ex B ). The {$1000.00} has not been applied towards escrow due, instead it has been held in suspense accounts and re-allocated. Per CFPB rule 1026.41, the amount due, has shown more prominently than other disclosures on the page and, if the transaction has multiple payment options, the amount due falls under each of the payment options and CFPB rule. Furthermore, the rule states that the monthly payment amount, including a breakdown showing how much, if any, will be applied to principal, interest, and escrow and, if a mortgage loan has multiple payment options, a breakdown of each of the payment options along with information on whether the principal balance will increase, decrease, or stay the same for each option listed must be shown. Since there is a lack of transparency in the negative escrow accounting, we are requesting that all payments be reallocated and applied to the negative escrow amount currently listed as {$21000.00}. CFPB Rule 1024.17 also has standards listed that must be adhered to in relation to escrow. if a servicer advances funds for a borrower, then the servicer must perform an escrow account analysis before seeking repayment of the deficiency. Proper analysis is not being performed to bring the escrow account out of delinquency.

In XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX, I contacted Banner Bank to have my PMI payment removed as I believed I qualified since houses on my block were selling in the high XXXX, which was higher than the fair market value range I needed to get my XXXX removed. Removing the PMI payment was very important to me because I had two XXXX XXXX XXXX and had not been able to work as much as I had previously. Removing the PMI would have been a huge relief for me and I was extremely excited at the prospect of it being eliminated. Unfortunately, the first BPO value was flawed and a second corrective BPO had to be done, at Banner Banks expense, as they ultimately took responsibility, but only after I had to fight to prove to them that it was their fault that I was unable to appeal the first BPO, causing a new one to be required. Still, the corrective BPO which revealed my true home value took nine months to get due to the errors, mismanagement, misconduct, unwillingness to help. The overall incompetence on the part of the two Banner staff members, XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX, resuled in me paying thousands in unnecessary PMI and interest on a higher principal during the months it took for Banner to process the corrective BPO. Not to mention the change in market which no doubt had an impact on the new BPO which was ultimately done in XX/XX/XXXX. It is the relief from those unnecessary PMI, and higher interest payments, that I am seeking today since it took almost a year of my life to deal with, and monitor, this situation while these staff members refused, then slowly, attempted to correct their mistakes and get on top of the matter. It isnt my job to do this, but it was theirs. I believe they paid for the corrective BPO in part to cover their legal exposure since I pointed out their errors in writing. While on the phone, XXXX was very clear - and insistent- that it was not their problem, or error to repair, and they would not be taking any steps to make things right. As I expected, the new BPO came back XXXX higher than the first flawed BPO. Because of this difference, I was able to pay down the {$2400.00} difference to get from 75.7 % LTV to 75 % exactly in order to successfully have the PMI removed. In early XX/XX/XXXX, I paid the {$2400.00} to have the XXXX XXXX monthly PMI payment removed from my regular mortgage payment. Despite the pay down amount not being applied to my regular mortgage payment, it was worth it to have all the money going to me rather than the banks insurance company. While any one of these things may have been minor, it is the sum total of these mistakes that has resulted in an unreasonable and unfair loss of money for me, and for which I would like Banner Bank to remedy. However, XXXX, on behalf of Banner Bank, doesnt care to acknowledge how this protracted XXXX month process due to her errors and foot dragging resulted in nine unnecessary PMI payments, and additional interest, while she got her act together to get the 2nd corrective BPO completed. XXXX dismissiveness is the reason I am opening a ticket here. I truly feel someone else needs to step in to make my reasonable request for reimbursement for the nine PMI payment happen, and to monitor these agents in order to prevent future harm to other Banner Bank clients. If it were not for them, I would have had a smooth and succinct BPO process, as is typical. Going back to how this all started. in XXXX XXXX, I was working with XXXX who took my information, agreed I was eligible based on the other requirements to remove my PMI, and set me up for a BPO. At that time, she took the money out of my account to pay for the BPO. I was told I would be contacted in about a week to schedule the appraisal. I waited and waited. Eventually a broker contact me for the BPO but he was rushed, told me the deadline was the next day, and he needed to come by asap to get it done. I accommodated. Weeks passedagain, no information or updatesfinally I contacted XXXX who said that the letter had been sent out a month prior but provided no additional information. I got the letter in the mail a few days later with a date confirming the decision was from a month prior and the PMI removal was denied. Reviewing the BPO it was clear that it was not accurate. The BPO did not use relevant comps and did not include any improvements made to the house. I contacted XXXX and told her that I would like to appeal the BPO, which XXXX approved, but XXXX did not tell me about this appeal deadline, nor did she inform me of all of the requirements. When I requested to appeal, XXXX told me I just needed to provide it in writing. No other information was told to me, required of me, and I was informed it was being processed. Then more time passed. I figured it took so long to get the first BPO that I didnt expect this process to be fast either. After a while though I asked XXXX what was going on. She told me the appeal request was denied two days after it was processed and I was sent a letter, but that I would need to file a new appeal if I wanted it done. I informed her that I did not get a letter about the appeal denial, nor did she call me, email more or follow up in any sense. Annoyed, but just wanting to move on, I told her to provide me the denial letter and all the information I needed to submit so I could get it done asap. No Response. I followed up again, no response. Eventually, I was connected to XXXX XXXX, XXXX, as XXXX was not communicating. XXXX emailed to tell me the appeal deadline had passed, rudely said it was my fault, and not their problem if I didnt get the letter, and if I want to pay for a new BPO I could pay to do that but otherwise I was XXXX This email was an attempt to get me to look past their misconduct. Unfortunately for them, I know my rights from working at law firms, and having deadlines, necessary paperwork and details withheld for me is not within those rights. After much back and forth, I was finally provided the document I had supposedly been sent but I never received. However, this document showed me that my appeal was not in fact denied- it was denied pending that additional requirements be provided - the ones XXXX never informed me of before submitting my appeal, or afterwards. The same documents I could have, and would have, provided if I was informed they were needed. This document itself did not go into detail of what was necessary, and it also did not include a deadline for these pieces to be submitted for appeal. Even if I had received it, it would not have given me all relevant information needed to avoid missing the appeal deadline. Once I pointed out that no where on the letter did it say there was a 120-day deadline to appeal, or provide any mention of a deadline, in writing did they approve the new BPO. Of course they acted like they chose to do it for me out of generosity which couldnt be further from the truth. There were no good faith efforts put forth by XXXX. As I asked XXXX, how is one supposed to meet a deadline they are not informed of, or submit documentation they were not told were required? The answer is - one cant. I was set up for failure by Banner Bank employees, and then they continued to fail me once caught. That, to me, is unacceptable. Especially since it is very likely it is not just me this is happening to. If XXXX wasnt following up with me to see if I got everything, or still wanted to appeal, then she is probably not doing that for other clients. And XXXX, while not the one to make the original mistakes, made the situation go from bad to atrocious with her defensive and couldnt care less approach. XXXX lack of concern, or willingness to remedy, acknowledge or apologize for the fact that her team cost a client thousands in unnecessary payments, nor did she provide me the proper numbers or calculations- which I am stil waiting for since my first letter - mailed only- had incorrect numbers, and no calculations, regarding what my new monthly payment will be. The continued lack of attentiveness, and laziness, as well as XXXX XXXX XXXX behavior, is the reason I am opening this CFPB ticket. Not everyone is willing to stand up for themselves like I am and I worry how her bullying could harm others as it harmed me. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and knows banks so she was able to help advocate for me, but not everyone has that. Enough is enough. Having been a manager in legal, advocacy and customer service settings, I know the first step to making something right is to acknowledge the problem, empathize and offer something to make them feel better. Especially if it is something small for the business overall. This was not the approach taken, I was instead bullied, insulted, gaslit and robbed by XXXX and XXXX Banks actions. And I would like for them to remedy the damages instead of saying sucks to be you. In fact, XXXX exact words on the phone - before I was able to prove to her in writing that I was right and which got me the new BPO covered- were ummm yeah were not going to do any of those things you suggested because its not our fault, its yours. It was that moment that I decided I would stand up for myself, and others, who are being misled by these two random people who work for the bank. Especially since they are supposed to help us succeed, and the approach taken suggests it is not only me being taken advantage of. Other than my one phone call with XXXX, I made sure all communication was in writing so that I could document what was happening. To Preface this, the lender is well aware of the situation since I have persued legal action against them. By way of introduction theres a Department of Veteran Affairs document online ( VA Form 26-8978 ) that outlines certain rights that VA loan borrowers have, including that you may sell your home to someone who agrees to assume your loan if the loan holder or VA approves the creditworthiness of the purchaser ( s ). It also mentions that these rights apply to the borrower and, if you sell your home, to any buyer who assumes the loan. On XX/XX/2022, I signed a contract to assume a VA loan. In order to complete the assumption process we ( me the buyer and the sellers ) had to work with the loan holder or lender. The lender then made the determination that I was not credit worthy and denied the assumption on XX/XX/2022. The VA does have some safeguards in place meant to protect the sellers and buyers in my situation, or at least give us some recourse in the event the buyer is denied the assumption. In the Lenders Handbook - VA Pamphlet 26-7 Chapter 5.6.h. Decision Notices The VA mandates that in the event an assumption is disapproved the disapproval notice from the lender must include a notice that the lenders decision may be appealed to VA within 30 calendar days, This is a safeguard put in place by the VA to give an assumer a right to appeal, however unfortunately for me the lender never did give me the required notice that I could appeal their decision directly to the VA. As a result I was stuck, the lender refused to reconsider my application, and I had no idea I had the right to appeal the lender 's decision to the VA . Consequently, I lost the assumption deal and realized heavy financial loss along with opportunity cost due to the many months I spent working towards the assumption including trying to get the lender to follow the guidelines and grant me my rights therein which they failed or refused to do even after I pointed it out to them. I spent ~ {$30000.00} dollars pursuing litigation against the lender just to have a judge in Utah court rule that the lender had no duty towards me ( no duty in tort ( negligence ) for this relationship between Defendant and Plaintiff ) to follow the established VA guidelines. Thus my concerns are two fold, 1. If a lender can not be held accountable for not following guidelines meant to protect those transacting in VA loan assumptions then that puts the public at risk both civilian and veteran alike when pursuing VA loan assumptions from abuse of power by the lender, homes are big life changing deals/purchases. 2. I lost a lot of money, hopes, and dreams etc.. Due to the lender 's negligence, I am looking to recoup what I lost from the lender, to hold them accountable and set an example so that other lenders think twice about taking lightly or ignoring these guidelines. The Lender is Cross Country Mortgage, and the above is just a brief summary of the situation. They also took 49 days just to get us our assumption application, and violated other VA guidelines such as retaining the full {$300.00} + dollar processing fee when the guidelines specifically say to return {$50.00} in the event an assumption is not completed. etc.. And wrongly indicated to me that I needed to owner occupy the property in order to assume it. I have additional evidence detailing all my correspondence with the lender. Please reach out if you would like more information regarding my experience. The lender failed in their responsibilities throughout the whole process, chief among those is that the lender violated my rights by not notifying me of my right to appeal their decision to the VA.

Time and time again, financial firms negligent handling of consumer data in conjunction with a lack of basic information systems security results in data breaches. Without any accountability or penalties there is no incentive for adequate investment in security. Rather, costs saved by not implementing these basic measures fatten bottom lines while exposing consumers to immense risk and potential harm. It is incumbent upon the CFPB, FTC and other agencies to increase enforcement until the costs of a data breach become incentive to properly safeguard this sensitive information. It is also essential that notice of past breaches be made centrally available to inform consumers. This information would go a long way toward guiding consumers to firms that are capable and careful with their data as the paltry offers of credit monitoring are insufficient to redress the harm caused by this negligence.

As you can see from the above chain of documented events SNSC was in clear violation of Regulation X dual Track Foreclosure laws in that they were secretly scheduling the auction of this properly all the while giving us false and misleading information as if they were in fact negotiating with us in good faith. I would ask the court to impose severe sanctions against this servicer as a means to deter them from this illegal act to other homeowners. I would also ask for your honor to also order them to conduct a meaningful short sale review and to actually submit documents to the investor. The offer that was submitted to the SNSC was rejected and the SNSC agent indicated that they wanted an amount that was in excess of fair market value. Again XXXX XXXX advised that the offer would still be rejected without ever going back to the investor with that new higher offer amount. We have been processing this short sale in excess of the 30 or 35 days prior to the sale as required under dual track foreclosure laws. Regulation X, implemented by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) pursuant to the Real Estate Settlement Procedure Act ( RESPA ), governs the handling of mortgage servicing, including loss mitigation and foreclosure proceedings. It establishes certain rights and responsibilities for both borrowers and servicers, with the objective of promoting fair and transparent practices in the mortgage industry. RESPA supersedes state law via the Supremacy Clause of the United States. Section 1024.41 of Regulation X specifically addresses the procedures and requirements for evaluating and responding to borrowers loss mitigation applications. It stipulates that once a complete application is received, the servicer must acknowledge the receipt in writing within five business days. Furthermore, the servicer is required to exercise reasonable diligence in obtaining all necessary documents and evaluating the application for a loss mitigation option. During this review process, foreclosure proceedings, including the scheduling of an auction date must be stayed. These actions by SNSC SERVICING is the textbook scenario why Dual Track Foreclosure laws were enacted. To stop banks from selling a homeowners home while at the same time reviewing them for work out options. The failure to cancel the auction and to complete the short sale review directly contradicts the spirit and intent of Regulation X, which aims to provide homeowners with a fair opportunity to explore loss mitigation options before facing the dire consequences of a foreclosure auction. I write this letter in a good faith attempt to have the foreclosure auction date removed and for the short sale to be reviewed again in a fair and amicable manner

In XXXX vs XXXX, the XXXX held that the XXXX XXXX 's findings of fact were supported by competent evidence and that as a matter of law, " A party to a contract may not complain of the nonperformance of the other party where that performance is prevented by his own actions. A party can not take advantage of a condition precedent the performance of which he has rendered impossible. A party who deliberately prevents the fulfillment of a condition on which his liability under a contract depends can not take advantage of his own conduct and claim that the failure of the fulfillment of the condition defeats his liability. Delays and nonperformance while they amount to a failure to perform are excused where performance is prevented by the other party to the contract. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX. As this is adverse action, I should have received notice of DCU 's intent to close this account. No notice was received. My mortgage, XXXX checking accounts, XXXX savings accounts, money market account and credit card are with XXXX, and I am an outstanding customer who pays my bills on time, never missed a payment, maintain a strong XXXX XXXX and they can see by my deposits that my income has doubled since my husband died. They did not notify me of this adverse action as they should have. XXXX XXXX XXXX is very clear and states : ( XXXX ) When notification is required. A creditor shall notify an applicant of action taken within : Official interpretation of Paragraph XXXX ( a ) ( XXXX ). ( i ) 30 days after receiving a completed application concerning the creditor 's approval of, counteroffer to, or adverse action on the application; ( ii ) 30 days after taking adverse action on an incomplete application, unless notice is provided in accordance with paragraph ( c ) of this section ; ( iii ) 30 days after taking adverse action on an existing account; or ( iv ) 90 days after notifying the applicant of a counteroffer if the applicant does not expressly accept or use the credit offered. ( XXXX ) Content of notification when adverse action is taken. A notification given to an applicant when adverse action is taken shall be in writing and shall contain a statement of the action taken; the name and address of the creditor ; a statement of the provisions of section XXXX ( a ) of the Act ; the name and address of the Federal agency that administers compliance with respect to the creditor ; and either : ( i ) A statement of specific reasons for the action taken; or ( ii ) A disclosure of the applicant 's right to a statement of specific reasons within 30 days, if the statement is requested within 60 days of the creditor 's notification. The disclosure shall include the name, address, and telephone number of the person or office from which the statement of reasons can be obtained. If the creditor chooses to provide the reasons orally, the creditor shall also disclose the applicant 's right to have them confirmed in writing within 30 days of receiving the applicant 's written request for confirmation.

On XXXX XXXX, XXXX, I applied for a cash-out refinance from Wells Fargo XXXX I have banked with Wells Fargo for 23 years. At the time I applied, I owed approximately {$8000.00} on a first mortgage with a different lender and had no other liens on my property. Market value of my property according to XXXX was approximately {$800000.00}. I have a house and barn on XXXX acres of woodland and fenced pasture bordered by a year-'round creek XXXX miles south and west of XXXX, Washington XXXX My house was built in XXXX. I requested a {$120000.00} cash-out refinance. I told the first loan officer I spoke with, XXXX XXXX, that I was requesting the refinance for the purposes of home improvement and to pay off debt. I told her I needed to repair my roof which was original to the house and XXXX XXXX XXXX. Wells Fargo required me to pay for my appraisal upfront, a total of {$990.00}. I was told this amount was not refundable after the appraisal had taken place. I paid Wells Fargo this amount. I was conditionally approved for the cash-out refinance on XXXX XXXX. I produced every one of a multitude of documents requested by Wells Fargo, including reams of documents from the local auditor 's office required to satisfy underwriters that I had recorded well , road maintenance and easement agreements. Many documents Wells Fargo required were private and requesting them seemed intrusive, but having had a XXXX relationship with Wells and knowing they already had access to my bank records, I provided the documents as requested and hoped for the best. I spent many hours researching and providing the requested documents. Despite my need for a new roof, my homeowners insurance agreed to rewrite my policy at Wells Fargo 's ( repeated ) request ( Wells contacted my insurance agency multiple times about this, something my agent said was unusual ) to provide 100 % wind and hail coverage. The newly-issued policy showed Wells as loss payee and was sent to Wells Fargo . Wells Fargo knew I had adequate homeowners insurance coverage. I sent loan officers copies of my contract for a new roof scheduled to be replaced XXXX XXXX, XXXX, along with receipts showing I had made a good faith down payment. As promised, my roof has now been replaced, as of XX/XX/XXXX. The appraisal took place on XXXX XXXX. The appraiser appraised my home at {$710000.00}, despite noting that I needed a new roof, that a beam beneath my upper deck had rotted and needed to be replaced, and that the siding on my home " should be checked '' although issues with my siding, he said, were " cosmetic. '' The appraiser also noted I needed a second strap on my water heater and a plug-in carbon monoxide detector, the latter two items costing less than {$100.00}. The appraiser estimated that replacing the roof, staining the siding and replacing the beam in the deck would cost approximately {$30000.00}. Wells Fargo then told me that I would have to complete all repairs before my loan could close. Loan officers told me underwriting suggested that I ask the contractors to agree to complete the work but to wait to be paid from the title company after all of the work was completed. Wells Fargo also told me that all of the work done would have to be inspected at my expense. I told Wells Fargo that in the XXXX XXXX, siding can not be stained or painted until summertime because weather conditions do not allow for it. Their requirement meant that I would have to ask roofers and the deck contractor to do their work but wait until summer, six months away or longer, to be paid. My application was sent to underwriters for a secondary review. The new underwriters agreed that all of the work would have to be completed and inspected before my loan could close. It is not reasonable to ask roofers and other contractors to perform work for which they can not be paid for six months or longer in order to await weather conditions favorable for painting.The appraiser did not state that the siding on my house was damaged, dangerous or deficient, only that it should be " looked at '' because of " cosmetic '' issues, yet Wells was stating that closing of my loan hinged on the siding being stained. I applied for a comparatively small mortgage, {$120000.00}, on a house appraised at {$710000.00}, even with needed roof and other repairs. I satisfied all of Wells Fargo 's requests for information and had a conditional loan approval. I have a long relationship with Wells Fargo. I have no overdrafts to my checking account and have never been late on a Wells Fargo credit card payment. I do not have a single late payment on my credit report. I provided evidence to loan officers that my roof was scheduled for replacement. I am now out countless hours of research and negotiations along with {$990.00} for this appraisal. I have had my privacy invaded also. Wells Fargo should tell applicants upfront when they are applying for a cash-out refinance for the purpose of home improvement that their underwriters may require necessary repairs and inspections for which they will be required to pay before any loan will close. Failing to disclose this information seems deceptive and misleading. At the very least, Wells Fargo should include appraisal and inspection fees in closing costs and not require them upfront before closing.
